title: Where the norm sits
summary: Why a pre-norm block trains more easily at depth.

choices.text: Pre-norm replaces layer norm with batch norm over the sequence, and batch norm is stable at this depth.
Pre-norm normalizes the residual stream after every block, so activations cannot grow with depth and the gradient through the stack stays bounded.
The skip connection stays a plain identity, so a gradient of 1 reaches earlier layers without being multiplied by the norm's Jacobian.
Post-norm applies the norm only once, after the final layer, so the earlier layers train on unnormalized inputs and need a long warmup to settle.
